So tonight is the first concert for the New School Studio Orchestra for this academic year or this season, and this has been a long time coming. First of all, the composer for tonight, you'll hear all the music that you hear will be from the great, great jazz and commercial music composer Oliver Nelson. And yeah, I mean really legendary and for a little while overlooked maybe, but never overlooked by the jazz community, and really one of the most powerful voices as both a tenor player, an alto player, small group, big band writing, and then into TV and film later. And an incredible body of work wrote as much as nearly any jazz composer wrote in their career and died at a tragically young age of 43. And so we have this body of work that was explored, of course, when he first wrote it because everybody wanted to play Oliver Nelson charts. And then as in some respects gone neglected, but tonight, especially this piece, The Kennedy Dream, I'm not sure I've not been able to find a live performance of this piece. So the only performance I've been able to find is the initial recording, which is incredible, but I'm sure someone in the interweb will find something and correct me and please do and send it to me. But this may be the world premiere of live performance of Oliver Nelson's Kennedy Dream. He wrote this in 1967, and it was the last piece that he wrote. He was living in New York, had a band, had been having an incredible amount of success while he was here on the East Coast, but he was headed to Los Angeles. And this was the last piece that he wrote when he lived here in New York. And then moved to Los Angeles, formed a new band, and wrote for film and television. And those of you who are into 70s TV for episodes of Colombo, and super classic, amazing TV of film music. So all of that super fun to hear, maybe hear a piece for the first time live. And then we're bookending the concert with maybe his most famous piece, Stolen Moments, which came from the album Blues and the Abstract Truth. And then the final piece, which comes from the Down by the Riverside, which comes from the incredible record with Jimmy Smith in West Montgomery. And so, you know, all in all, I'm excited for you all to hear this. I hope you're excited. I'm excited as well. I want to thank Nick Marchione and Ed Newmeister for conducting the group for this last five weeks and preparing them for the concert. I want to thank all the musicians and actors from the College of Performing Arts. This is a truly collaborative effort, musicians from the School of Jazz and Contemporary Music, from the Manus School of Music, and actors from the School of Drama here at the New School. And so with that, please welcome Nick Marchione and the New School Studio Orchestra.
